comment: Read from the maker's source at commit 3a9441f. The 39 tempo marks are a literal array in Metronome.cpp. The one-step-slower input has an off-by-one: the code reads if (--bpmIndex <= 0) bpmIndex = 38, so stepping down from the second mark, 42, lands on 208 rather than on 40, and 40 can never be reached from that jack. Stepping by two or three uses a subtraction loop and wraps correctly at the top. The timer only runs inside a test on the output being connected and the start button being on, so an unpatched metronome counts nothing. The tempo display and the numbers printed round the dial are drawn by the module and are not controls. The start button is a large round switch at the centre of the tempo knob; both can be clicked, the switch answering at the middle and the knob around it.
